topic: Perioperative SGLT2 inhibitors and 7-day postoperative AKI (randomized trials)
clinical_question: Do perioperative SGLT2 inhibitors reduce KDIGO-defined AKI within 7 days after adult cardiac surgery versus placebo/standard care?
primary_endpoint: AKI within 7 postoperative days (KDIGO stage ≥1 or equivalent)
rationale: Clinically central, mechanistically plausible, and most consistently reported. Four RCTs report this endpoint or near-equivalent windows; definitions largely KDIGO-aligned; effect data are available or reported as RR.
clinical_coherence: High (perioperative timing; similar surgical contexts; AKI captured within 5–7 days)
methodological_coherence: High (restricted to RCTs; separable from observational evidence; compatible effect measures)
publication_value: High—recent large multicenter RCT plus supportive smaller RCTs; substantial readership interest and practice relevance
major_limitations: One RCT provides RR without raw counts (SCR_000098) | Exposure regimens vary (chronic preop with periop hold vs 1–3-day periop dosing) | One RCT used composite KDIGO/AKIN/RIFLE definition

topic: Preoperative SGLT2 inhibitor exposure and 7-day postoperative AKI (observational cohorts)
clinical_question: Among adults undergoing cardiac surgery, is preoperative SGLT2 inhibitor exposure associated with reduced KDIGO-defined AKI within 7 days versus nonuse?
rationale: Multiple adjusted cohorts with compatible early AKI windows; valuable as sensitivity/triangulation separate from RCTs.
clinical_coherence: Moderate (urgent/emergent vs elective; exposure windows differ)
methodological_coherence: Moderate (adjusted RR vs adjusted OR; entropy weighting vs PSM; mix of 48 h vs 7 d windows)
publication_value: Moderate—useful corroboration but confounding remains; best framed as secondary evidence
major_limitations: Effect measures not uniform (RR vs OR) | Time windows vary (48 h vs 7 d) | Residual confounding likely despite causal methods

topic: Euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis (eDKA) in the immediate postoperative period
clinical_question: Does perioperative SGLT2 inhibitor exposure increase the risk of biochemically confirmed euglycemic ketoacidosis in the first 24–72 hours after cardiac surgery?
primary_endpoint: Biochemically confirmed postoperative ketoacidosis within 24–72 hours (acidosis + ketones; specify euglycemia threshold)
rationale: Clinically important safety concern; conflicting signals (zero events in several RCTs vs high incidence when systematically sampled in one cohort).
clinical_coherence: Low—definitions and ascertainment strategies vary widely; some rely on symptomatic testing only
methodological_coherence: Low—zero-event pairs common; heavy detection bias; different biochemical thresholds and sampling schedules
publication_value: Moderate (safety signal worth discussing), but meta-analysis currently unjustified
major_limitations: Inconsistent definitions and sampling windows | Zero-event patterns | Potential duplication of perioperative policies (drug holds) not harmonized

topic: Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) after cardiac surgery
clinical_question: Do perioperative SGLT2 inhibitors reduce MACE after cardiac surgery?
primary_endpoint: MACE at a uniform timepoint (preferably 30 days, RCTs only)
rationale: Important but sparse and heterogeneous (30 days vs 1 year vs 5 years; varying definitions)
methodological_coherence: Low—mix of RCT vs long-term observational designs; composite definitions differ
major_limitations: Heterogeneous timepoints and composite definitions | Insufficient trials reporting a common window
